newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian coalition backs deputy PM ahead of inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Belgian coalition backs deputy PM ahead of inquiry.

text.p: Members of the four parties forming Belgium's ruling coalition said on Thursday that Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo could stay in his job during a court investigation of child sex allegations against him.

"For me personally I see no reason to tell Di Rupo that he must resign," Tony Van Parys, a member of the Flemish christian democrat CVP party, told reports after a meeting of a parliamentary commission assessing the allegations. The CVP is the largest party in the centre-left coalition.
Van Parys was one of 11 members of a parliamentary commission which on Thursday decided to recommend to parliament not to send Di Rupo before court over the allegations.

The commission, made up of representatives of the main political parties, wants the Cour de Cassation, the highest court in the land, to make further investigations into the allegations and to submit a report by December 9 at the latest.

Asked whether Di Rupo could continue with his work until the report, commission member Serge Moureaux, like Di Rupo a francophone socialist, said: "The case against Di Rupo is not complete enough to warrant an immediate resignation." He added: "It is an embryonic case...very unconvincing."
Commission member Renaat Landuyt, a member of the Flemish SP socialist party, told Reuters, "It would be very unfortunate if Mr Di Rupo would have to resign at this stage,"
